title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 51
paragraphs: After this Artabanus said: “O king, since you urge us to fear nothing, let me ask you to accept one more piece of counsel from me — for when so many things are in question, the discussion must necessarily be longer. Cyrus son of Cambyses subdued all Ionia except the Athenians and made it tributary to the Persians. These men, I counsel you, you should by no means lead against their parent stock, seeing that even without them we are able to get the better of our enemies. For if they go with us, either they must prove themselves great wrongdoers by joining in the enslavement of their mother city, or great righteous men by joining in freeing her. If they show themselves great wrongdoers, they bring us no great advantage besides; but if they show themselves great righteous men, they are capable of doing much harm to your army. Take to heart, then, the ancient saying, how well it was said, that at the very beginning of things the end does not fully appear.”
